title: meridian-docks-chatops-integration-notes
content:
Context: quick field notes after kickoff call w/ Meridian Docks (terminal operator; heavy chatops for dock dispatch + container routing). They want LLM-driven assistant for dispatchers and ops supervisors inside existing Slack + on-prem cockpit (web app behind corporate VPN). Primary ask: real-time contextual suggestions (ETA adjustments, routing hints), slotting rules, natural-language search over manifests.

High-level constraints they emphasized:
- P99 latency target: <= 120ms tail for suggestion endpoint when used inside Slack (very sensitive).
- Batchiness: lots of small interactive requests; cannot add >50–80ms extra latency for batching.
- Data residency: full manifest data stays on their VPC; logs must be scrubbed before anything leaves private environment.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + EU data residency; optional HSM/KMS integration for keys.
- Availability: need graceful degradation to cached heuristic rules if model unavailable.
- Cost sensitivity: big daily volume spikes during vessel arrivals; they prefer predictable billing (reserved capacity) over bursty usage.

Current topology they run: on-prem Kubernetes cluster (2 GPU nodes at pilot), internal Slack workspace, Postgres for manifests + S3-compatible object store for images. They will consider a dedicated VPC deployment or a hybrid (control plane hosted, runtime in customer VPC).

Notes from call (raw):
- Meridian (CTO: Elena Rousseau, Eng lead: Harish Menon) care about 1) latency 2) control over PII 3) predictable monthly cost
- They showed a demo of their Slack workflow where dispatchers hit a slash command /suggest and expect near instant reply with 2–3 short suggestions
- Example prompt flow: short container ID -> fetch manifest rows -> produce 2 concise routing options with confidence score + policy flags (hazmat, size restrictions)
- They asked about model memory (session context): need per-incident KV cache for the last 30 minutes of messages plus manifest prefix caching
- Hard requirement: all manifest text and IDs must never be sent to hosted model unless encrypted and authorized (prefers runtime in their VPC)

Redwood-specific recommendations (initial):
1) Private deployment (VPC) with runtime inside customer's subnet + control plane hosted. This meets residency & data residency ask while minimizing lift.
2) Dedicated capacity pools for the Slack suggestion endpoint to guarantee tail latency and predictable billing during vessel windows.
3) Use prefix/KV caching for manifests: store manifest vectors and token prefix KV cache with TTL 30m to reduce tokenization and recomputation.
4) Routing policy: low-latency route -> local dedicated pool; fallback -> smaller quantized model in same VPC (if capacity low) -> final fallback -> local heuristic microservice to keep UX alive.
5) Quantization recommendation: start with int8 for candidate model to save GPU memory; but run eval on their sample prompts to verify hallucination risk.
6) Streaming vs sync: keep suggestion endpoint sync (no SSE) to avoid partial suggestions; but implement streaming for longer explainers (post-accept).

Technical gotchas / open questions (to clarify with customer):
- How large are manifest text blobs on average? (they said "mostly short lines, some long notes up to 8k chars") -> will impact sequence length and kernel selection
- Slack rate pattern: concurrent 80–200 requests per minute in peak windows? Need precise spike shape for autoscale config
- Are there internal heuristics currently used we can import as a fallback microservice? (Harish said yes, a python service with business rules)
- Does customer have existing HSM keys / KMS we need to integrate during pilot? They mentioned Azure Key Vault but uncertain about HSM
- Acceptable data-retention window for logs/trace? They asked for 7-day rolling traces for debug, but legal might require longer for incidents

Operational runbook ideas (short):
- Canary rollout: route 5% traffic to Redwood model variant A (full precision) + 95% to their existing heuristics for first 72h, collect quality metrics via prompt set (we need to prepare ~200 labeled prompts)
- Evaluate quality using Precision@1 and hallucination incidents flagged by dispatchers; tie an SLO to % of unacceptable responses per 1k prompts
- Autoscale: maintain baseline reserved tokens to cover 90th percentile; allow burst to pre-provisioned spot capacity for arrivals windows

Proposed next steps (owner + date):
- Asha: send summary + ask for manifest sample (anonymized) and Slack usage histogram (due 2024-11-11)
- Tom: draft pilot architecture diagram (control-plane hosted, runtime VPC, networking + mTLS details) and attach Terraform snippet for VPC peering (due 2024-11-13)
- Maya: build short eval harness with 200 prompts (customer-supplied + seeded) and run model quality sweep across 3 quantization profiles (float16, int8, q4) — initial report due 2024-11-20
- Harish (customer): confirm HSM/KV approach and provide contact for infra team; also give sample traffic histograms by 2024-11-12

Notes-to-self / internal follow-ups:
- Need to confirm whether P99 120ms includes network RTT to Slack and back — likely they measure end-to-end; we should instrument synthetic client to replicate.
- Prepare a short doc on "fallback semantics" for dispatchers so UX degrades gracefully (e.g., explicit banner if model low confidence)
- Cost modeling: compute cost per suggestion for float16 vs int8 vs q4 and include amortized reserved pool cost in pilot proposal

Unresolved UX decisions:
- Where to show confidence/trace? inline text vs modal. Customer prefers inline but worried about clutter
- Retry behavior when model returns low confidence: immediate second call to quantized fallback vs show heuristic suggestion

Potential risks:
- If manifest blobs often hit >4k tokens, we might need longer sequence kernels or chunking + retrieval approach -> affects latency
- On-prem GPU ops team inexperienced with quantized runtime troubleshooting; may require extra on-call support during pilot (bridge support)

Useful links mentioned on call:
- Slack thread: #mdk-integration (Harish)
- Confluence: MDK internal api spec -> CONFLUENCE:MD-API-SPEC
- JIRA epic: MDCK-112 (pilot)
